root_cause.text: The st_lsm6dsx IIO driver exposed the buffer sampling frequency sysfs attribute for all sensor types, even though st_lsm6dsx_hwfifo_odr_store() ultimately indexes a 2-entry odr_table by sensor->id, causing out-of-bounds access for non-accelerometer/gyroscope sensors.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE/commit explicitly states that st_lsm6dsx_hwfifo_odr_store() calls st_lsm6dsx_check_odr(), which accesses odr_table at index sensor->id even though "this array is only 2 entries long," and the fix changes st_lsm6dsx_fifo_setup() to pass st_lsm6dsx_buffer_attrs only for ST_LSM6DSX_ID_ACC and NULL for other sensors.

intent_record.intent_summary: Restrict FIFO sampling frequency buffer attributes to the accelerometer so only it can expose independent FIFO rate control.
intent_record.what: Inside the loop in st_lsm6dsx_fifo_setup(), a new local variable `const struct iio_dev_attr **attrs` is introduced, assigned to `st_lsm6dsx_buffer_attrs` only when `i == ST_LSM6DSX_ID_ACC` and to `NULL` otherwise, and the call to `devm_iio_kfifo_buffer_setup_ext()` is changed to pass `attrs` instead of always passing `st_lsm6dsx_buffer_attrs`; a comment explaining the accelerometer-specific behavior is also added.
intent_record.how: At runtime, only the accelerometer IIO device gets the extra buffer attributes that expose FIFO sampling frequency controls, while other sensors no longer receive those attributes. This enables configuring the accelerometer FIFO data rate independently of its sensor sampling rate and prevents unrelated devices from exposing unsupported or inappropriate FIFO sampling frequency settings.

grouping_result.intent: Restrict FIFO sampling frequency buffer attributes to the accelerometer so only it can expose independent FIFO rate control.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly addresses the root cause by limiting the FIFO sampling frequency sysfs attributes to the accelerometer, preventing unsupported sensor types from reaching code that indexes the 2-entry odr_table by sensor->id and causing out-of-bounds access.

candidates.rationale: This loop applies buffer setup across all sensor IDs, causing the FIFO sampling frequency buffer attributes to be exposed for sensor types beyond accelerometer/gyroscope, which enables the later out-of-bounds index by sensor->id.
This call installs the common extended buffer attributes for every present IIO device, directly exposing the FIFO sampling frequency sysfs attribute to unsupported sensor types.
As part of the per-device buffer setup call, this line participates in registering the buffer interface for all sensor IDs, including those that should not have independent FIFO rate control.
This passes the shared buffer attribute set, including the vulnerable sampling frequency sysfs attribute, to every device created in the loop, which is the direct exposure bug.

vuln_statements.explanation: This call registers the extended buffer attributes for every IIO device iterated in the loop. Because the shared attribute set includes the FIFO sampling frequency sysfs attribute, it exposes that control to unsupported sensor types, leading to later out-of-bounds indexing by sensor->id.

This argument supplies the common buffer attribute set containing the vulnerable sampling frequency attribute. Passing it for all devices is the direct mechanism that exposed the unsafe sysfs entry to non-accelerometer/gyroscope sensors.

This loop applies buffer setup indiscriminately across all sensor IDs, expanding the vulnerable attribute exposure beyond the supported sensors and enabling the later invalid sensor->id indexing path.

As part of the same buffer setup call, this line participates in registering the buffer interface for every sensor instance in the loop, contributing to the unintended exposure of the shared buffer attributes.

Author: Francesco Lavra <flavra@baylibre.com>
Date:   Fri Oct 17 18:42:55 2025 +0200

    iio: imu: st_lsm6dsx: Decouple sensor ODR from FIFO batch data rate
    
    The rate at which accelerometer or gyroscope sensor samples are fed
    to the hardware FIFO (batch data rate, or BDR) does not have to

bic_trace_step.reason: The diff is sufficient because it shows the newly added sysfs buffer sampling_frequency attribute and the exact store handler logic. The vulnerable construct is present: `st_lsm6dsx_hwfifo_odr_store()` is added and exposed through `st_lsm6dsx_buffer_attrs` / `devm_iio_kfifo_buffer_setup_ext(...)`, which makes the buffer `sampling_frequency` attribute available for every `hw->iio_devs[i]` in `st_lsm6dsx_fifo_setup()`. There is no filtering by sensor type or sensor id before exposing it. The root cause says only accelerometer/gyroscope are valid because lower-level ODR handling indexes a 2-entry table by `sensor->id`; this function directly calls `st_lsm6dsx_check_odr(sensor, hwfifo_odr, &data);` with no guard restricting `sensor->id` to accel/gyro. Thus for non-accelerometer/gyroscope sensors, the vulnerable path remains reachable. The fix is not present because there is no conditional hiding of the attribute, no validation such as restricting to accel/gyro IDs, and no alternate safe handling for other sensor types.
